assumptions: The continuous wheel-speed, vehicle-speed, slip-ratio, and PID computations are treated as plant/controller logic outside this discrete supervisor; the FSM consumes the already-computed slip-error/PID-derived input `slp` used in the specified guards.
The initial state is `increase` because it is the first state named in the natural-language state list and no alternate initial hierarchy was provided.

transition guards split the slip-error space ... when `slp <= 0.01`, `slp > 0.01`, `slp < -0.01`, and `slp >= -0.01`
`increase` sets `k1=1`; `hold` neutralizes both valves with `k1=0`; `decrease` sets `k1=0`
`increase` sets `k2=0`; `hold` neutralizes both valves with `k2=0`; `decrease` sets `k2=1`
`increase` sets `n=0`; `hold` sets `n=0`; `decrease` sets `n=500` to release pressure

M1_guard_off_by_one.description: guard `>= N` mistakenly written as `>= N-1` (fires one cycle too early)

M2_wrong_transition_target.description: transition `A -> B` written as `A -> C` (wrong target state)

M3_unreachable_target.description: guard threshold set far too high (`>= 99999`), target state never reached

M4_missing_forced_transition.description: forced transition `! ...` line missing (global event ignored)

M6_wrong_effect_value.description: effect assigns wrong constant (`var = N` → `var = N+100`)

canonical_scenario_results.description: default-init verifies the initial transition dispatches to increase and sets inlet/return/pump outputs for pressure increase.
canonical_scenario_results.name: default_init_enters_increase_outputs

canonical_scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start probes the inclusive slp <= 0.01 guard from increase to hold and then verifies hold does not leave at exactly 0.01.
canonical_scenario_results.name: increase_to_hold_at_positive_boundary

canonical_scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start probes the strict slp > 0.01 guard from hold to increase and confirms increase does not transition to hold when slp is just above 0.01.
canonical_scenario_results.name: hold_to_increase_above_positive_boundary

canonical_scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start probes the strict slp < -0.01 guard from hold to decrease and confirms decrease does not transition to hold when slp is still below -0.01.
canonical_scenario_results.name: hold_to_decrease_below_negative_boundary

canonical_scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start probes the inclusive slp >= -0.01 guard from decrease to hold and then verifies hold does not enter decrease at exactly -0.01.
canonical_scenario_results.name: decrease_to_hold_at_negative_boundary

canonical_scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start verifies the deadband case slp=0.0 keeps the supervisor in hold with both valves and pump neutralized.
canonical_scenario_results.name: hold_deadband_zero_stays_neutral

evidence: NL states: increase sets k1=1, k2=0, n=0; hold sets k1=0, k2=0, n=0; decrease sets k1=0, k2=1, n=500.
DSL enter actions implement the same assignments for increase, hold, and decrease.
NL guards: increase->hold slp <= 0.01, hold->increase slp > 0.01, hold->decrease slp < -0.01, decrease->hold slp >= -0.01.
DSL transitions implement those four guards exactly.
findings.summary: The DSL faithfully captures the explicitly specified three-state hydraulic supervisor, including state names, valve/pump assignments, and slip-error threshold guards.

evidence: inspect_model_to_json_summary.metrics.n_states_leaf = 3.
inspect_model_to_json_summary.transition_count = 5, including the initial transition and four normal guarded transitions.
variables_sample includes slp, k1, k2, and n.
action_count = 3, corresponding to state entry output actions.
findings.summary: Required supervisor components are covered: all three named states, all four named guarded transitions, the slip-error variable, and the three output targets k1, k2, and n.

evidence: NL says wheel speed and vehicle speed are used to compute the slip ratio, and the PID output drives the Stateflow supervisor.
DSL declares only slp, k1, k2, and n; there are no wheel speed, vehicle speed, slip-ratio calculation, PID state, or PID output variables.
GroundingMap source_summary assumes continuous wheel-speed, vehicle-speed, slip-ratio, and PID computations are outside the discrete supervisor.
findings.summary: The model does not represent wheel-speed/vehicle-speed slip-ratio computation or the PID controller; this is acceptable only if the review scope is limited to the discrete Stateflow-style supervisor consuming an externally computed slp.

evidence: Diagnostic W_UNWRITTEN_READ_VAR reports slp is read but never written.
Diagnostic W_GUARD_VARS_NEVER_CHANGE appears on all four guarded transitions reading slp.
design_diagnostics_summary.inspect_summary.nl_external_input_vars includes slp.
Diagnostics W_UNREFERENCED_VAR for k1, k2, and n are consistent with output-only variables rather than control-state variables.
findings.summary: The variable roles are implicit: slp is declared as an initialized internal-looking variable but is actually used as an external input, while k1, k2, and n are pure outputs. This causes advisory diagnostics but does not contradict the NL.

evidence: Core required FSM states, transitions, guards, and output actions are present and simulation scenarios pass.
sim_summary reports 6 scenarios passed out of 6.
The broader NL mentions PID coupling and wheel/vehicle speed slip computation, which are not modeled in the DSL.
five_component_summary is empty, limiting independent component-level assurance.
findings.summary: Estimated NFRR tier is T3 for the discrete hydraulic supervisor, but not T4 and potentially capped to T2 if the intended target is the full ABS/PID/plant model rather than just the FSM supervisor.

evidence: sim_summary scenarios cover initial increase output, positive boundary, above positive boundary, negative boundary, below negative boundary, and deadband hold behavior.
No scenarios mention wheel-speed input, vehicle-speed input, PID calculation, or hydraulic plant dynamics.
five_component_summary is empty.
findings.summary: The simulation oracle appears adequate for the listed supervisor thresholds and outputs, but it does not evaluate full ABS/PID behavior or plant interaction.
